# Neuro & Evil Karaoke API — QR code sign-in

Base URL: https://api.neurokaraoke.com (Production)

For devices with a screen but no convenient keyboard (TVs, desktop apps, kiosks). The user approves the sign-in from a phone that is already signed in.

1. The device calls `POST /api/auth/qr-session` and displays the returned QR code.
2. The device waits for approval through `GET /api/auth/qr-session/{sessionId}/events`, or polls `GET /api/auth/qr-session/{sessionId}`.
3. The user scans the QR code on a signed-in phone and confirms. The phone calls `POST /api/auth/approve-qr`.
4. The device receives `status = approved` together with the bearer token.

Sessions expire after 5 minutes. Create a new session when the old one expires.

### `POST /api/auth/qr-session` — Start a QR sign-in session

Auth: none

Creates a QR sign-in session for the calling device. No request body.

The response contains `sessionId`, `approveUrl` (the URL to encode in the QR code), `qrCodePayload` (same value), `qrCodeImageDataUrl` (a ready-to-display PNG data URL), `statusStreamUrl` and `expiresAt`. Display the QR code, then wait for approval with `GET /api/auth/qr-session/{sessionId}/events` or by polling `GET /api/auth/qr-session/{sessionId}`.

Treat `sessionId` as a secret. Anyone who has it can collect the token after approval.

Response `200` OK `application/json`:

```ts
{
  sessionId: string | null
  approveUrl: string | null
  statusStreamUrl: string | null
  qrCodePayload: string | null
  qrCodeImageDataUrl: string | null
  expiresAt: date-time
}
```

### `GET /api/auth/qr-session/{sessionId}` — Get QR sign-in status

Auth: none

Returns the status of a QR sign-in session. `status` is `pending` until the user approves, then `approved` with the bearer token in `token`. Returns `404` when the session does not exist or has expired. When polling, wait at least 2 seconds between requests.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sessionId` | path | `string` | yes |  |

Response `200` OK `application/json`:

```ts
{
  status: string | null
  token: string | null
  expiresAt: date-time
}
```

### `GET /api/auth/qr-session/{sessionId}/events` — Stream QR sign-in status

Auth: none

Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`) alternative to polling. Each event's `data` is a JSON object with `Status`, `Token` and `ExpiresAt`. Note the PascalCase property names, which differ from the camelCase names returned by the status endpoint. The stream sends the current status immediately, sends a heartbeat comment every 15 seconds, and closes after the `approved` event or when the session expires. Returns `404` (as JSON) when the session does not exist.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sessionId` | path | `string` | yes |  |

Response `200` OK

### `POST /api/auth/approve-qr` — Approve a QR sign-in session

Auth: `Bearer`

Called by the signed-in user's device after scanning the QR code. Approves the session in `sessionId` and hands the caller's sign-in to the waiting device. Returns `404` when the session is invalid or expired. Clients should always ask the user to confirm before calling this.

**Requires a bearer token.**

Request body `application/json`:

```ts
{
  sessionId: string  // min length: 1
}
```

Response `200` OK `application/json`:

```ts
{
  status: string | null
  token: string | null
  expiresAt: date-time
}
```

Response `401` Missing, invalid or expired credentials.
